benefits: Supervision and mentoring of local training
eligibility: Citizen of an OIC member state
Employed by a research institution in an OIC country
Working in any area of the biomedical sciences
At least an M.S. in Biomedical/Health Sciences or equivalent for graduate studies, or a Ph.D. in Biomedical/Health Sciences for post-graduate studies
Age limit: maximum 35 years for graduate studies, 45 years for post-graduate studies
Applicants may apply for only one COMSTECH programme per calendar year
requirements: Match the published field: virology, genetic engineering or infectious diseases
Complete the official application form and email it with all attachments to COMSTECH Headquarters, Islamabad (khazima@comstech.org or comstech@comstech.org)
Scanned copy of passport, even if expired, showing the page with name and surname
CV of maximum five pages, including publications

Supporting statement from the head of the home institution, plus two reference letters from senior scientists familiar with the applicant's work (the head of the home institution cannot be one of the referees)
M.S./Ph.D. degrees and relevant university transcripts

Scanned copy of passport, even if expired (page with name and surname)

selection_criteria: Fellowships are awarded by COMSTECH, along with the Host Institutions Joint Fellowships Committee
Preference is given to young scientists, particularly women scientists, at the beginning of their research career
Preference is given to those working in Least Developed OIC Countries (LDC), or from Muslim majority areas in non-OIC states
coverage: Subsistence at the host institution (provided by the host institution)
Supervision and mentoring of local training (provided by the host institution)
application_method: Complete the official COMSTECH application form
Assemble the required supporting documents and email the completed form and attachments to khazima@comstech.org or comstech@comstech.org
Applications are jointly reviewed by an expert committee of COMSTECH and the host institutions
official.application_route: Complete the COMSTECH application form and email it with all supporting documents to COMSTECH Headquarters, Islamabad (khazima@comstech.org or comstech@comstech.org); a joint COMSTECH-host institution committee reviews the file.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of OIC member states who are employed by a research institution in an OIC country; the fellowship funds a visit to a centre of excellence in another OIC country.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. All eligible applicants are citizens of OIC member states and the fellowship is explicitly for visits to designated centres of excellence in an OIC country other than the applicant's own.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Field must be virology, genetic engineering or infectious diseases; hosting is through COMSTECH Consortium of Excellence (CCoE) member institutions across OIC member states.
official.research_requirement: The application form requires a written statement of research/training objectives, describing in at least 200 words the research or training the applicant wishes to conduct; no full research proposal is specified.
official.description: COMSTECH, in collaboration with key centres of excellence in OIC countries, offers fellowships to young scientists in OIC countries to enable them to spend three months at a relevant centre of excellence in an OIC country other than their own. The stated purpose is to enhance the research and development capacity of promising scientists, especially those at the beginning of their research career, and to build capacity in virology and vaccine technology for current and future pandemics.
official.region: OIC-wide (Africa, Middle East and Asia); hosting country is various higher education institutions in OIC member states including Pakistan
official.program_type: Inter-governmental research and advanced training fellowship

verification.notes: Full call text, terms of fellowship, eligibility, documents and application route were read directly on the official COMSTECH call page, together with the official jotform application form it links to and the CCoE host-institution list. No monetary amount, stipend figure, tuition waiver or closing date is published anywhere on those official pages; the promotional flyer for the 2024 round carries a 'Fully Funded' badge and a different age band, but publishes no figure, so it is not treated as evidence of a funded stipend.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a three-month research and advanced-training visit, not a degree scholarship: you keep your home-institution post and travel to a designated centre of excellence in another OIC country, with COMSTECH covering international low-cost airfare and the host expected to provide subsistence, supervision and mentoring. No stipend amount, tuition coverage or closing date is published, so budget for the gaps and do not wait for a deadline announcement. Because only one COMSTECH programme may be applied for per calendar year, choosing this one closes every other COMSTECH route for that year.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career biomedical scientists in virology, genetic engineering or infectious diseases, aged 35 or under (45 for post-doctoral level), employed at a research institution in an OIC country, who want hands-on vaccine and diagnostics training abroad for three months.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the head of your home institution's written endorsement first; that same person is barred from being a referee, so line up two separate senior referees early.
Trim the CV to five pages maximum including publications, and prepare a legible scan of the passport data page (expired passports are accepted, illegible scans are not).
Compress every upload to the form's hard limits (300 kb per PDF/JPG attachment, 500 kb for the CV) and refresh the CV so it reflects the last six months.
Draft both 200-word statements (motivation, and research/training objectives) and name up to two preferred CCoE host institutions, accepting that placement elsewhere is possible.
Email the completed package to both khazima@comstech.org and comstech@comstech.org so a single mailbox outage cannot lose your file.
common_rejection_risks: Applications or supporting documents submitted in French are explicitly not considered for evaluation, so a non-English or incomplete file can be turned away without review.
Naming the head of your own institution as a referee is an automatic disqualifier under the published rules.
Age is screened at 35 for graduate studies and 45 for post-graduate studies, so candidates near the boundary can be excluded before merit is even weighed.
Field mismatch: the call is limited to virology, genetic engineering and infectious diseases, so a strong applicant in an adjacent biomedical discipline can still be ruled out.
Applying to a second COMSTECH programme in the same calendar year makes the applicant ineligible for both.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published package is international airfare plus host-provided subsistence only; visa fees, insurance, personal expenses and any salary shortfall during the three months away are not covered, and no monetary figure or subsistence rate is published so the depth of the host's support cannot be checked in advance.
document_audit: The passport scan must show the name and surname page; an expired passport is fine but a cropped or low-resolution scan is the classic failure.

The form rejects files above 300 kb for attachments (degree/transcript, reference letter, passport) and above 500 kb for the CV, so scan at moderate resolution instead of attaching a multi-megabyte camera photo.
The call page caps the CV at five pages while the form asks for a 'detailed' CV; staying inside the cap is safer than assuming either limit dominates.
Two separate senior referees are required and the institution head's supporting statement cannot count as one of them.
Degrees and transcripts must both be supplied, not only the highest certificate.
alerts: No closing date is published: the call is simply marked open, so there is no window to plan against and the practical move is to submit as soon as the file is complete.
One COMSTECH programme per calendar year, so accepting this fellowship blocks other COMSTECH fellowships and scholarships for that year.

The 2024-round promotional flyer claims 'Fully Funded' and lists a different age band (28-40) plus observer-state eligibility; the live call page states 35/45 for OIC member states only and publishes no figure, so rely on the call page, not the flyer.
A passport valid for travel is still needed for the visa even though an expired copy is accepted with the application itself.
Host placement is not guaranteed even when two preferred CCoE institutions are named.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill in the online form, attach the scanned documents within the file-size limits, and email the completed package to COMSTECH Headquarters, where a joint COMSTECH-host institution expert committee reviews it and awards on scientific merit.
